_doc: PLATFORM-BRIEF-1: the platform-neutral description of Ultrastable, handed to a cloud platform's own AI agent so it works out the deployment. We state WHAT must exist and WHICH loops must close; the platform's agent decides HOW on its own services. Source of truth for site /deploy.md and docs/PLATFORM-BRIEF.md (generated by scripts/platform_brief.py).
intro: Ultrastable is a system that runs itself: a scheduled tick reads work items, assigns them to roles (doer and independent reviewer), opens and merges its own code changes, measures the result, and keeps or reverts the change. People only contribute ideas in plain language.

requirements.need: Serve a public website and a read-only dashboard over HTTPS on a custom domain.
requirements.probe: GET / returns 200 and /health returns the deployed version equal to the repository version

requirements.need: Run a scheduled function every 10 minutes (the tick) with no server to maintain.
requirements.probe: a tick row is written within 15 minutes of deploy

requirements.need: A relational database (SQLite-compatible or Postgres) for the work ledger, trust ledger and metrics.
A key-value store and an object store for assets, caches and state snapshots.
requirements.probe: a written key reads back identical bytes

requirements.need: Run an AI agent step: call a hosted model, with tool use, from the tick. The model provider may differ from the cloud.
requirements.probe: one issue produces one pull request

requirements.need: A secret store that only the runtime can read; no secret is ever written to the repository.
requirements.probe: secret names listed, values never printed

requirements.need: Send and receive email for the owner digest and double opt-in subscribers.
Deploy only through the repository: pull request, green checks, merge, then deploy and verify live.

loops: work: issue -> role assigned -> draft pull request -> independent review -> merge -> deploy -> verify live
measure: change states predicted metric movement -> deploy -> metric re-read -> keep or revert
heal: probe fails -> issue and draft pull request opened by itself -> owner and closing probe attached -> fix merged -> probe passes
bootstrap: one idea in plain language -> project created -> site deployed -> live probe passes, no code touched by the person

ask: Using your own services and best practices, propose the smallest deployment that satisfies every requirement, then perform it. Show the plan first in plain words. Do not delete or overwrite existing resources. After deploying, run each probe and report the real output. Where you cannot satisfy a requirement, say which one and why; do not substitute silently.
